input: logs is an Array of at most 100 ASCII strings, each length 3 through 100. Each has a nonempty identifier and at least one content token, separated by single spaces without leading/trailing spaces. Identifiers are ASCII alphanumeric; each content is uniformly lowercase-letter words or uniformly decimal-digit words, not mixed. Empty logs is accepted. Integer inputs, when present, are primitive safe-integer Numbers excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays without holes, proxies, subclasses or accessors; strings are primitive. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: A fresh Array of the original immutable log strings: all letter logs first, ordered lexicographically by full content then identifier, followed by digit logs in their original order. Exact letter-key ties additionally preserve original index order explicitly, independent of sort stability.
mutation_aliasing: All input values, caller containers and ordering remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state and separate calls share no mutable result state. Content/identifier slices, sortable private letter records and a private digit list are allocated. Input logs is never sorted or changed; only output references to original immutable strings are returned.
numeric: All text ordering uses ASCII, so Python and JavaScript lexicographic comparison agrees. Original indices are small safe integers and act as a final deterministic tie key. The first content character is sufficient to classify a log only because the uniform-content precondition holds.
complexity: Let N be log count, L letter count and C<=100 the maximum string length. Partition/slicing costs O(N*C). Python sorting costs O(L*log(L+1)*C) comparison work and O(L) key/work slots; JavaScript sorting costs T_sort(L,C) time and S_sort(L) workspace depending on runtime. Private records/slices plus result storage cost O(N*C+S_sort(L)) in JS and O(N*C) in Python. Returned text is not regenerated.
